# JAMES L. CLARK

STUDIO

949 HOME STREET, BRONX

NEW YORK CITY

May 22nd, 1914.

5/30/144

Col. Theodore Roosevelt,

oyster Baew York.

My dear Col. Roosevelt:

Regarding the three lion rugs which were

returned to me for repairing:

I am enclosing you several photographs of

lion head which I have mounted

for the wall and with which

I have been very successful;

several men having sent me

their lion rugs to put into this shape. I offer these as a suggestion for the rugs that you have returned, since to

after two attempts, it seems impossible to find any way teep your lion rugs from wrinkling;

as I have said before,

is due to the original tanning.

In mounting these heads for the wall the

body skin is not cut away, but tucked inside the head and shoulders.

The mounts are much more satisfactory in appear-

ance than the rugs inasmuch as they are more natural, the main difference is that the skin gets now ware such as it is subject to on the floor.

I would strongly advise that your rugs be

made into similar mounts, and would be very glad to hear from you regarding this.

I am under the impression that there is

something to be fixed on the elephant tusk gong; if this is so, I would be glad to fix it whenever you so desire.

With congratulations for you recent success-

full trip and with kindest regards, I am

Kindly let me know

Vexy respectfully yours,

whether the shipment

Xlar

arrived
